checks.command: python3 plan/check.py && python3 plan/selftest.py && python3 tools/program.py --verify && python3 tools/guides.py --verify && python3 -m unittest tools.test_capability_ledger
checks.output: Plan integrity, all 12 selftest drift cases, generated program and guide verification, and 105 Python tests pass offline. No network access, no secret and no new runtime dependency; the checker imports only the standard library and plan/baseline.py.

review.acceptance: primary-session self-review only; not independent, and no second reviewer examined this slice

extra_checks.name: Lease correction
extra_checks.output: R0-16's epic-default lease excluded docs/, so it could not edit the one ledger its own counter measures. The lease was corrected in its own prior commit, judged by the policy at that base, before this work was claimed. R0-08 carries the identical defect and was corrected in the same commit.

extra_checks.name: Fixture honesty
extra_checks.output: All 117 fixture cells record 'none — GATE-ORACLE' rather than a path. A test fails if any row claims a fixture while GATE-ORACLE holds fixture capture closed, so the counter cannot be satisfied by inventing fixture references.

notes: Ticket assignment is family-level: each capability section is keyed to the contract item that defines that family, which is the true granularity available today because per-capability implementation items do not yet exist. Owner is the crate the target architecture assigns the family to. Both are recorded as measured assignments, not placeholders, and the checker enforces that every ticket resolves. No subagent was launched: the work is one ledger rewrite plus its checker, and this session was operated under an instruction not to spawn agents.
